title: Release Pathflow: compact onboarding visuals for canary / A-B / fallback policies
creator: Maya Chen
description: Scope: Design a compact ‘Release Pathflow’ quickstart that introduces engineers to pinning model versions and configuring progressive rollouts. The flow must cover three core patterns: 1) Canary (small % traffic with auto-increase gates), 2) A/B (split routing with metric comparator), and 3) Fallback policy (automatic switch to a safe variant on errors/latency/regression). Assets will include three annotated screenshots for the Console, an explainer overlay sequence for first-time users, a lightweight illustrator for each pattern, and a compact policy editor mock. Purpose: reduce time to first successful canary rollout and minimize post-release confusion about pinning and fallback behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Three annotated Console screenshots (Canary wizard, A/B split summary, Fallback policy editor) exported at 2x for retina and available as editable Figma frames
A 4-step overlay micro-tour that appears on first use explaining traffic %, metric gates, and rollback triggers
Design tokens and responsive specs (desktop/tablet) documented in the Figma file and handed off to frontend
Accessibility checks: contrast, keyboard focus order, screen-reader labels for policy toggles
Sign-off from PM (Priya Raman) and Eng owner (Liam O'Neal) recorded in comments
deliverables: Figma file: Release Pathflow - compact tour (editable frames)
Confluence quickstart doc draft with screenshot callouts
Component spec doc for Console engineering (colors, spacing, microcopy)
tasks: Draft initial wireframes for three patterns (Maya)
Prototype micro-tour overlay and animation timings (Maya)
Sync with ENG to validate feasible editor controls and validation states (Ethan + Liam)
Run accessibility audit and adjust contrast/labels (Maya)
Export assets and create PR with screenshots for docs (Ethan)
Localization pass for Spanish/DE/JP microcopy (PM to coordinate)
decisions: Use a compact 4-step overlay instead of full-page walkthrough to keep onboarding opt-in and low friction
Expose only primary safety knobs in quickstart (traffic %, metric, rollback window); advanced knobs moved to an 'Advanced' panel
Prefer a single fallback toggle with prefilled safe variant suggestions (based on historical success rate) rather than free-text selectors in the initial release
tradeoffs: Concise overlay reduces learning depth — mitigated by linking to an expanded doc in the overlay footer
Choosing prefilled fallback variants may surface recommendations that are imperfect for edge cases; keeps UX simple for 80% of users
A/B split visualization simplified to percent bars to avoid clutter; advanced metric comparators deferred to later iteration
accessibility_notes: Ensure all controls have aria-labels, include live region announcements for rollout state changes, verify color contrast >=4.5:1 for core badges, and provide keyboard-only flows for the policy editor. Include alt text for all exported images in the docs PR.
localization_notes: Microcopy strings isolated in the Figma token layer. Reserve 30% expansion space for German and Spanish. Provide a short context note for translators describing 'fallback' as fallback model variant on error/latency/regression.
